claim: Proper nonconstant smooth algebraic varieties with a regular top-form seed have no nonzero constant compact exponential period.

inspected_statements.content: The graph seed delta(t-f) belongs to V^{>0}, from negativity of Bernstein-Sato roots. Nonconstant f on the irreducible source excludes the identically zero germ.

inspected_statements.locator: Theorem 8.1, printed pages 41-44; complete four-step proof inspected
inspected_statements.content: For a smooth projection proper on the module support, filtered relative de Rham direct image injects into ordinary direct image and gives its canonical V-filtration.
Submodules and quotients have induced V-filtrations; D-module morphisms are filtered and strict.
A module supported on t=0 has V^alpha=0 for alpha>0.

application_hypotheses.source: Smooth irreducible algebraic surface after proper graph modifications.
application_hypotheses.map: Proper and nonconstant to the affine phase line; proper on graph-module support.
application_hypotheses.seed: Original normalized algebraic residue two-form, proved regular on the resolved model.
application_hypotheses.period: The original compact real sphere, retained unchanged by the boundary modifications.
application_hypotheses.module: H^0 f_+ O_Y with the actual top-degree relative de Rham seed; no parameter-dependent gauge.
application_hypotheses.convention: Decreasing V^alpha; the positive level contains the seed and vanishes on the point quotient.
application_hypotheses.critical_loci: No isolated-critical-point or semisimplicity hypothesis is used.

derived_argument: The proper filtered direct image places the volume seed at a positive V-level. A nonzero constant period gives an unlocalized cyclic Fourier quotient to O_tau, hence an inverse-Fourier quotient to delta_0 carrying the seed to its generator. Strict V-filtrations force this image to vanish, a contradiction.
scope_limit: This source supplies the stated V-filtration facts. Boundary resolution, seed extension and the eleven-parameter polynomial certificate are proved separately in the canonical source.
